title: Congruence of atomic evaluations
statement: Let $C_w,c_w\in\mathbb{N}$, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, and let $z,z'$ be finite Boolean words. Suppose their six decoded components—representing the input, description, time word, auxiliary word, index word, and final word—agree componentwise. Then every atom over the states and work tapes of $M$ has the same Boolean evaluation on $z$ and $z'$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
The decoded input components of $z,z'$ agree
The decoded description components of $z,z'$ agree
The decoded time-word components of $z,z'$ agree
The decoded auxiliary-word components of $z,z'$ agree
The decoded index-word components of $z,z'$ agree
The decoded final-word components of $z,z'$ agree
$a$ is an atom over the states and work tapes of $M$
